title: Celine Dion Makes Record-Breaking $125 Million Comeback in Paris
summary: The first leg of her French residency wrapped with historic results.
contentText:
The last time Celine Dion was on tour, she and her fans alike were unaware that concert venues (and the rest of the world) were about to close completely for more than a year. The Courage World Tour kicked off in September 2019 and generated more than $100 million before hitting pause in March 2020. On the other side of the COVID-19 shutdown, Dion delayed her return several times before officially canceling the remainder of the tour in 2023 due to her diagnosis with stiff-person syndrome. But don’t fret: Three years later, Dion is back and bigger than ever with record-breaking Boxscore figures.

Related

Céline Dion’s Comeback: 5 Takeaways From Night Two Of Her Paris Residency

According to figures reported to Billboard Boxscore, the first leg of her residency, titled Celine Dion Paris, wrapped with $125.5 million and 539,000 tickets sold across 16 shows in September and October. Her comeback residency is anchored at Plenitude Arena in Paris (fka La Defense Arena).

A single-venue residency is known territory for Dion. A New Day… (2003-07) and Celine (2011-19), both staged at The Colosseum at Caesars Palace in Las Vegas, are the two highest grossing residencies in Boxscore history. The former grossed $385.1 million in 714 shows, and the latter brought in $296.2 million in 427 dates.

While Celine Dion Paris has yet to crack the top 10 of the highest grossing residencies, its 16 shows highlight how impressive the nine-figure gross is. On a per-night basis, her 2026 dates averaged $7.8 million — more than 10 times the nightly take from either of her Vegas stints. That surpasses U2 ’s Sphere residency, which grossed $6.1 million per show to become the fastest grossing residency ever. (Residencies are defined as 10 or more shows at a single venue. Extended stays within a larger tour — such as Harry Styles at Madison Square Garden during Together Together or Shakira in Madrid during the Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran World Tour — do not count).

Further, Dion’s average crowd of 33,700 is close to double the next best per-show attendance for any residency in the Boxscore archives. ( Billy Joel paced 18,600 tickets during his tenure at Madison Square Garden.) When she claimed her throne in Vegas in the 2000s and 2010s, the most competitive residency venues were The Colosseum at Caesars Palace and MGM’s Dolby Live, topping out at 4,000 and 5,200 seats, respectively. Las Vegas’ Sphere has since blown the door open for arena-sized residencies, selling upward of 15,000 tickets each night for Backstreet Boys , Dead & Company , Eagles and more. While Dion’s Plenitude Arena is technically an indoor arena, its capacity is stadium sized.

Dating back to a December 1990 performance at Montreal’s Theatre St-Denis, Dion has grossed $1.3 billion and sold 9.8 million tickets from a reported 1,517 concerts. More than half of that, in terms of gross, attendance and number of shows, stem from her three residencies.

Dion is slated to return to Paris next year with 10 shows from May 8 to 29, likely to sell her 10 millionth ticket — and then some.
